en: If the President vetoes a bill, Congress can still make it a law if two-thirds of both houses vote to override the veto.
When Spanish authorities discovered the secret Katipunan society, members tore their cedulas to physically symbolize their violent break from colonial taxation and rule.
Ifugao farmers carve stone-walled canals to channel natural mountain springs, which continuously flood their terraced paddies to grow rice year-round.
Dr. Fe del Mundo designed a bamboo incubator where jars of hot water provide steady radiant heat to keep premature babies warm.
Devotees perform the Sinulog dance by taking two steps forward and one step back to mimic the flowing current of the Pahina River.
Because the first eight provinces rebelled against Spain, Emilio Aguinaldo placed eight rays on the flag's sun to represent these specific regions.
Kalinga tattoo artists tap soot mixed with sugarcane juice into the skin using calamansi thorns, which permanently embeds the dark pigment.
When a presidential candidate receives the highest number of regular votes nationwide, Congress officially proclaims them as the winning President.
When speakers of different regional languages communicate, they use Filipino as a lingua franca, which bridges their linguistic differences and enables mutual understanding.
After electing representatives from liberated towns, the Malolos Congress drafted a constitution that officially established the First Philippine Republic with a president.
By pressing an elder's hand to their forehead, a younger Filipino performs the mano po gesture, which physically demonstrates their deep respect.
To protect against earthquakes, traditional bahay kubo houses use flexible bamboo poles and lightweight nipa leaves that sway instead of collapsing.
